trust_decision.summary: On receiving a COOKIE-ECHO, the worker's SCTP Association decides whether the State Cookie is one it generated itself. At the pinned commit this check covers only magic values and length (no MAC, no timestamp), so on non-DTLS transports (Plain/Pipe) a forged cookie creates a TCB and moves the association to ESTABLISHED.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'state cookie lacks authentication / unauthorized association establishment'. HandleReceivedCookieEchoChunk is where the cookie is parsed and the TCB is built from it.

fix_sites.entry_point: PlainTransport/PipeTransport UDP/TCP SCTP packet -> Transport::ReceiveSctpData -> Association::ReceiveSctpData (Node API router.createPlainTransport/createPipeTransport({enableSctp:true}))
received INIT chunk on the same transports (HandleReceivedInitChunk)
fix_sites.module_kind: core protocol state machine (cookie producer side)

fix_sites.entry_point: transport creation with enableSctp (worker channel request from Node/Rust API)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: worker/src/RTC/SCTP/association/StateCookie.cpp:83-122 and worker/src/RTC/SCTP/packet/parameters/StateCookieParameter.cpp:118-149 (cookie serializer, called from INIT handling at worker/src/RTC/SCTP/association/Association.cpp:1567, not from the COOKIE-ECHO check). The per-transport policy wiring at worker/src/RTC/PlainTransport.cpp:40 and worker/src/RTC/PipeTransport.cpp:32 is the second out-of-package part.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: 'The bug is in COOKIE-ECHO validation.' A solver can harden Parse/IsMediasoupStateCookie (for example, check tags or state) without touching the INIT-ACK producer, which is the only place that can embed a MAC/timestamp. They can also argue that Plain/Pipe SCTP runs between trusted mediasoup peers, or that WebRtcTransport is the only exposed surface.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate handshakes must keep working: a normal handshake, a duplicate COOKIE-ECHO (case D), INIT collision (case B), peer restart (case A) and a COOKIE-ECHO that arrives late but within the cookie lifetime. WebRtcTransport must keep plain 44-byte cookies. The published test also requires the default SctpOptions to still accept an unauthenticated cookie, so making authentication always on breaks the published test. Peer-implementation detection from cookie magic must keep working.

O6_input_shapes: authenticated 72-byte cookie with a valid MAC
authenticated-length cookie with a tampered MAC or bytes
authenticated cookie whose timestamp is stale (> ValidCookieLifeMs), answered with an ERROR/Stale Cookie
COOKIE-ECHO received with no TCB vs with an existing TCB (restart/collision path)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A packet whose first chunk is COOKIE-ECHO skips the verification-tag check, and when the cookie is rejected (parse failure, or MAC failure after the fix) the handler only returns, so bundled DATA/SACK/SHUTDOWN/RE-CONFIG chunks in the same packet are still processed against an existing TCB. RFC 9260 5.1.4 (quoted in the fix) says the whole packet must be discarded.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Verification-tag handling is a neighbouring feature (section 8.5.1), not cookie authentication. With no TCB, bundled chunks are dropped anyway by ValidateHasTcb.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point: the packet validation function and the chunk loop at worker/src/RTC/SCTP/association/Association.cpp:583-591, about 1100 lines away

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Put the MAC check only in the no-TCB branch, leaving the restart path (HandleReceivedCookieEchoChunkWithTcb case A, which tears down and rebuilds the TCB from cookie values) unauthenticated.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The two branches are already handled asymmetrically: the no-TCB branch has its own verification-tag check at 1716. A maintainer could plausibly add authentication next to that check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Have IsMediasoupStateCookie accept either length and Parse fall back to plain-cookie handling when the length is 44, letting a forged plain cookie downgrade past authentication.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix itself makes IsMediasoupStateCookie accept both lengths (fix.diff:650). A compatibility fallback is a natural thing to write.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Derive requireAuthenticatedCookie from an options flag (for example, isDataChannel) rather than the transport type, so that one transport kind ends up with it off.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The SctpOptions are built in the shared base constructor from FBS options, and the policy is just a bool passed by each subclass.

O9_family: CWE-345 insufficient verification of data authenticity (missing MAC on a server-issued stateless token / SCTP State Cookie)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Tighten StateCookie::Parse/the COOKIE-ECHO handler, for example by requiring a TCB or state COOKIE_WAIT or matching tags, instead of adding a keyed MAC and timestamp at generation time. This either breaks the passive-side handshake or stays forgeable.

unverified: O8 route: the claim that bundled chunks are processed after a rejected COOKIE-ECHO with an existing TCB is from reading only (ValidateReceivedPacket returns true at 1179-1182; the loop at 583-591 continues because HandleReceivedChunk returns true at 1397). The individual handlers' tolerance of a mismatched tag was not traced.

Hidden tests in the fix diff use new API names (SctpOptions::requireAuthenticatedCookie, StateCookie::VerifyMac, AuthenticatedStateCookieLength, ValidCookieLifeMs). They would need rewriting as behavioural tests through the transport/ReceiveSctpData before they are fair to a solver who chooses a different design.
